page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n2d-standard-64 in the top 25% for several compute and memory metrics. It demonstrates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, alongside high Passmark CPU scores, particularly in encryption, physics, and extended instruction sets. Memory performance is strong for small-block cached read operations, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidth falls into the average category. In real-world application simulations, the instance achieves strong results in database operations, ray tracing, and image processing, while maintaining average throughput for static web serving and Redis SET operations.

For language model tasks, the instance delivers strong text generation speeds with small 135M models, but performance drops to the bottom 10% when running large 70B models, highlighting a clear limitation for heavy LLM workloads without GPU acceleration. Given its balanced resource distribution and strong multi-threaded capabilities, the n2d-standard-64 is highly suited for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that require high CPU density without specialized storage or accelerator hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with 32 physical cores, it provides a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs. In benchmark testing, the n2d-standard-64 delivers strong performance in multi-core CPU stress tests, database operations, and encryption tasks, placing it in the top 25% for these categories. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and static web serving throughput remain average. While highly capable for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and database hosting, it exhibits poor performance on large-scale LLM inference. This server represents a balanced, high-density compute option for standard enterprise workloads.
